$schemaNote: One entry per app. Required: id, name, repo, summary, about, technical, platforms, version, icon, screenshots, links. Allowed platforms: android, ios, windows, macos, web. Use "Unknown" for an unknown version and add a todo. screenshots[]: {src (WebP or PNG under static/), alt, width, height} (no captions); 0-4 per app, fictional demo data only. links.download may only point at github.com/<owner>/<repo> (archives, tags, releases) and is the only download rendered. links.githubRelease and links.ownDownload are reserved slots (see README, 'Download data model'): keep them null, or {"enabled": false, ...}, until a release reviewer approves; the build never renders them. links.iosAppStore is reserved for a future App Store listing (null until one exists). Live app URLs that are not on GitHub must NOT go here. about[]: plain-language paragraphs for non-technical people (what it does, why you'd want it; no stack or hosting jargon). technical[]: stack, hosting and requirements, shown last in Details. Never mix the two. updates[]: {version, date (optional, YYYY-MM-DD), notes[]} newest first, only from public release notes. builtWith: the AI model or service used to build the app, or null (hidden).

apps.name: Galaxy Gridiron
apps.summary: A read-only fantasy football companion for Sleeper leagues.
about: Galaxy Gridiron shows your Sleeper fantasy football leagues at a glance. Type your Sleeper username and it shows your teams across six tabs: Team, Matchup, League, Waivers, Trades and Picks. Tap any player to see his card, news and live stats during his game, or ask the chat button a question about your team.
It only looks, never touches: it can't change anything in your leagues and never asks for a password.

notes: Player ranks: a player's card shows his position rank by points per game and by total season points, in a plain sentence, and says when missed games explain the difference. The chat's player card shows the same ranks.

Cleaner Matchup screen: a short result pill ("Leading by X", with "Won by" only once every game is final), +/- chips, a compact report card with the rest behind "Details", and shorter live card labels.
Trade questions in the chat are fixed: asking who to trade for two named players now offers deals that give exactly those players, with the trade value math shown plainly.
Tips for dropping, picking up and trading players now count backup quarterbacks correctly.
A player's card shows his live points, projection and a stat breakdown while his game is on.
Your picks are banana yellow, so they no longer look like a win.
The picks leaderboard is now called "Picks by week" and shows the newest week first.
A repeated weekly chart and the video buttons were removed.

technical: Android app built with Expo / React Native (TypeScript). The iPhone version is a web app (PWA) export that you add to your Home Screen from Safari.
League data comes from Sleeper's public, read-only API. An optional Cloudflare Worker powers the AI chat, so the app itself never holds an AI key.

platformNotes.web: On iPhone, open it in Safari and add it to your Home Screen.

screenshots.alt: Galaxy Gridiron launch screen: football and planet emoji over a starry purple background, an empty Sleeper username field, a Launch button, and the note that the app is read-only and needs no password.
Tutorial card 1 of 7, Welcome to Galaxy Gridiron, explaining the six tabs (Team, Matchup, League, Waivers, Trades, Picks) and the chat button, with a Next button.
Tutorial card 3 of 7, Picks and leaderboard, explaining weekly NFL picks, your record and chart, and the shared leaderboard, with Back and Next buttons.

apps.name: Swipe Clean
apps.summary: Swipe through your photos to decide what to keep and what to delete.
about: Swipe Clean helps you tidy your photo library one swipe at a time: swipe left to put a photo in your Delete pile, right to keep it. Undo, combos and a daily streak keep it quick and fun.

It never deletes anything by itself and never picks photos for you. You look over your Delete pile, then remove those photos yourself with your phone's own delete prompt (or in Google Photos on the web). On the web you can try a demo with sample photos.

notes: Lil sits in the middle of the top bar on every screen, with room to hop and throw hearts, so Lil is never cut off (this also fixes Lil being clipped on Home).
The top bar has a soft rounded dip under Lil, in both themes. With "Show Lil" off, the edge is simply flat.
Bigger header labels and numbers, with more space from the side buttons. Still fits narrow phones.
Swipe screen top bar, left to right: Back, Photos (done/total), Lil, Minutes (today/goal), Pile. The deck date is now a small line under the progress bar.
Other screens use the same top bar, with a stat on each side.
Tapping Lil over and over always gets a fresh reaction; two small timing bugs are fixed.
New Settings > Appearance: Dark (default), Light (a warm cream look), or Match my phone.
Photos and videos always open on a dark background, even in Light mode.
New app icon: Lil holding a polaroid with two little hearts, next to a small light grey bin. Supports Android themed icons.
Meet Lil Guy, the mascot, who reacts to every choice with an equally happy reaction, so no choice is cheered more than another. Tap Lil for a reaction.
Idle poses: leave the screen alone for a few seconds and Lil briefly turns into a camera, film roll, polaroid peek, camera strap or photo frame.
Settings > Lil Guy: "Show Lil" and "Calm mode". Lil also stays still if Android's "Remove animations" is on.

technical: Android app built with Expo / React Native, with a small Kotlin module that talks to MediaStore and uses the system trash and delete dialogs.
The Web version is a browser demo for Google Photos using the Picker API with a read-only scope. It runs in demo mode with generated placeholder photos until you add your own Google OAuth client ID.

platformNotes.web: A browser demo with sample photos; connecting Google Photos needs extra setup.

apps.name: Kanban Board
apps.summary: A shared to-do board for two people that keeps working offline, with a TV mode.
about: Kanban Board is a shared to-do board for two people. Cards move through Ideas, To Do, Doing and Done, and each card can have a priority, an owner, tags, a due date and a checklist.

Everyone sees the same board: when someone adds, edits, moves or deletes a card, every open phone, computer and TV updates within about a second. If the connection drops, you can keep working and your changes catch up by themselves.

notes: A small self-hosted server (for example on a Raspberry Pi) stores the board in one file and sends live updates: every open phone, computer and TV shows the same cards within about a second.
Keeps working through connection hiccups; your changes catch up by themselves. A status dot shows Live, Reconnecting or Offline.
Each device asks once "Who are you?" (no passwords), using generic owner names.
Full-screen TV mode with big text and a clock, plus install scripts.
Backups are kept automatically. If two people change the same card while offline, the most recent change wins, and a deleted card stays deleted.
First version: a single-file Kanban board in the browser with Backlog, To Do, Doing and Done columns, due dates, priorities, tags, checklists and an owner field.
Saved on your device, with JSON export and import.

technical: A tiny Node.js server with no dependencies holds the one real copy of the board and pushes live updates to every open page. It keeps rolling backups (the last 30 versions, at most one every 5 minutes). Requires Node.js 18 or newer.
Runs in any browser; an open page queues changes while the server can't be reached. TV mode is the ?tv=1 address. The repo includes install, kiosk and watchdog scripts for a Raspberry Pi.

platformNotes.web: Runs in any browser; someone sets it up once on a small always-on computer.

apps.name: Cat Health Dashboard
apps.summary: A simple health log for your cats, with a weight chart for each cat.
about: Cat Health Dashboard is a simple health log for your cats. Record weight, food, water, litter box, behavior, symptoms, meds given and vet visits, keep track of upcoming appointments, and see a weight chart for each cat. Each entry shows who logged it.
Add it to your phone's home screen like an app and share one log between phones. It keeps working when you're offline.
Built for cats, with a litter box log and cat wording, but the entries are simple, so it can be adapted to other animals.

notes: Optional notes on pet profiles.
Upcoming appointments: add, edit or cancel them from a pet's page; they show on the home screen, and "Mark done" turns one into a vet-visit log entry.
Privacy hardening: the app asks search engines not to index it and doesn't send referrer information.
First release: a phone-friendly shared pet health log with a simple name picker and no logins.
Pet profiles and quick logs for weight, food, water, litter box, behavior, symptoms, meds given and vet visits, with a weight chart.
Symptom entries are flagged "check with your vet"; the app gives no medical advice.
Works offline, can be added to your home screen, and syncs between phones within seconds.

technical: A single-page web app (PWA) that installs on phones and caches data offline in the browser.
Syncs between phones through a here.now Site Data collection that you set up with your own config. Cats are added in the app; no data lives in the repo.

platformNotes.web: Add it to your phone's home screen; sharing between phones needs a one-time setup.

screenshots.alt: Cat Health Dashboard home on a phone: an Upcoming card with a dental check for Juniper, and two demo cats, Biscuit (5 years, male, 10.7 lb, last fed 4 hours ago) and Juniper (about 6 years, 13.1 lb, flagged symptom this week), with an Add a cat button.
Biscuit's page: profile line, an Upcoming section with an Add appointment button, eight log buttons (Weight, Food, Water, Litter box, Behavior, Symptom, Meds given, Vet visit) and a weight chart.
Biscuit's weight chart from early September to late October rising from about 10.2 to 10.7 pounds, then recent entries for food, water, behavior, meds and weight with their dates.
